page: The Vultr vhf-3c-8gb is an instance within the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 3 shared vCPUs on an x86_64 Intel processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The virtual machine includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 16 MB of L3 cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and support for instruction sets including AVX, AES, and FMA. Storage is bundled with a local 256 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance comes allocated with one complimentary public IPv4 address. No discrete GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinction between single-threaded efficiency and multi-core scalability. The instance demonstrates top-tier single-threaded gzip compression throughput at 38.09 GB/sec, alongside average middle-tier results in stress-ng single-core (2401.69) and multi-core (7120.84) testing. However, uncached memory bandwidth registers in the lower 25% bracket, with 32.54 GB/sec read and 16.94 GB/sec write speeds. High-concurrency operations also show constraints, as Geekbench multi-core (2928.0), software compilation via Clang (3982.0), and PassMark CPU overall (5738.4) place in the bottom 25% of measured systems. Inference benchmarks indicate workable speeds for small 135M parameter language models, but performance drops substantially on medium 7B models.

Given the shared vCPU model and bundled high-speed NVMe storage, the vhf-3c-8gb provides cost-efficient resource density for entry-level and utility services that do not require continuous multi-threaded execution. The configuration is appropriate for lightweight database operations, compression-heavy batch jobs, background tasks, and development environments. Because multi-core capacity and memory bandwidth are limited, it is less suited for heavy code compilation, high-volume web serving, or large-model artificial intelligence inference.
